content_blocks.code:
name: Validate pull requests
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: echo "Run non-privileged validation here"
content_blocks.expected_output: A pull request targeting `main` starts validation with read-only repository permission.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Open a harmless test pull request and confirm the run appears on its checks page. Do not add privileged deployment credentials to this job.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Close the test pull request and remove any temporary branch.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain pull request events, read the example, and identify a way to validate it. The wider system goal remains: Choose triggers and filters that run the right validation at the right time without exposing privileged jobs.

content.task: Apply pull request events to a small workflow change. State the expected result first, validate the configuration, then record evidence from the run or static check.
task_acceptance_criteria: Identify the relevant event, workflow field, runner behavior, or security boundary.
Explain the expected success result and at least one failure or skip condition.
Use least privilege and a disposable/test context; do not include credentials or production resources.

content.expected_output: The expected result is the behavior described here: Pull-request workflows validate proposed changes before merge and must treat forked or contributor-controlled source content as untrusted. The real result depends on the repository, selected ref, configured permissions, and runner availability.
troubleshooting: If a workflow never starts, verify the workflow is under `.github/workflows/`, the event and filters match, and repository/organization Actions policy allows it.
If a step fails, inspect the first failed step, exit code, stderr, installed tool versions, permissions, and runner/network state before retrying.
If a job is skipped or data is missing, inspect `if`, `needs`, outputs, artifact names/paths, and cache keys; jobs do not automatically share filesystems.
common_mistakes: Assuming YAML parsing proves the workflow runs correctly or matches the intended trigger.
Granting broad token permissions, printing environment values, or exposing a secret to untrusted code.
Using a placeholder command as evidence of a real build, test, deployment, or security scan.
